prerequisites: (FMFI.KEF/1-AIN-140/22 - Computer Principles - Hardware or FMFI.KI/1-INF-130/00 - Computer Architecture)
(FMFI.KAI+KDMFI/1-AIN-130/22 - Programming (1) or FMFI.KAI/1-AIN-105/22 - Efficient Algorithms and Data Structures)

learning_outcomes.text: Understand the principles of computer architecture at the level of machine code.
Be able to write simple programs in assembly language.
Be able to use typical operating system services in C programs.
Understand the concepts from the theory of operating systems: process management and scheduler.
Understand internal principles of how modern operating systems work.
Be able to apply the acquired skills in administration of operating systems and while developing applications.

syllabus_topics: Machine code level - specific example Intel® Pentium®
Selected services of operating systems from the point of view of application developer and their practical usage
assessment_rules: Students need at least 70% to pass practical exercises and 70% on the quiz. Extra bonus points can be earned for extra work. Evaluation is the same in both parts of the course.
bibliography: Mikroprocesory Intel Pentium a spol. / Michal Brandejs, available at http://www.fi.muni.cz/usr/brandejs/Brandejs_Mikroprocesory_Intel_Pentium_2010.pdf
Remzi H. Arpaci-Dusseau and Andrea C. Arpaci-Dusseau: Operating Systems: Three Easy Pieces, CreateSpace Independent Publishing Platform, 2018.
Andrew S. Tanenbaum and Herbert Bos: Modern Operating Systems, Fourth Edition, Pearson
